transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jamal (Redwood Product), Mark (CloudPeak CTO), Sara (CloudPeak PM), Benji (CloudPeak Eng)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
- Goal: align on technical steps to get Redwood listed on CloudPeak marketplace, finalize reference architecture and define joint solution ops/SLAs.
- Main concerns: network connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), SSO/SAML for listing, data residency and audit logs, packaging model runtime for marketplace (container vs AMI), monitoring and billing integration.
- Agreed next steps and owners, schedule follow-ups.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, appreciate you making time. Quick intros on our side, I'm Alex from Redwood partnerships, Priya is our SE and Jamal internal product owner.
[00:12] Mark (CloudPeak): Hey, Mark here, CTO, Sara's on for partner program, Benji on infra.
[00:18] Sara (CloudPeak): Yep hi all.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): Great, so agenda, marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture, joint solution flows and then open Q&A. We'll try to capture action items as we go.
[00:30] Benji (CloudPeak): Quick ask on the listing side — do you require us to host the model runtime or can Redwood host and we just surface the integration in the marketplace listing?
[00:38] Alex (Redwood): Good q. We support both. For marketplace-first go-to-market most partners prefer Redwood-hosted endpoints (hosted API) for fastest time to value; but we also support dedicated or private deployments where customers bring their own infra — that's pretty common for enterprise buyers. For the listing, we can have 'Hosted by Redwood' or 'Bring-your-own infra' options in the listing metadata.
[01:05] Mark (CloudPeak): Ah okay, good. If we go with hosted, what are the data residency / logs implications — our legal team will ask about where logs and telemetry land.
[01:15] Priya (Redwood): Right, we can do region pinning for hosted infra and we have audit logs and retention controls. For sensitive customers we recommend Redwood Private in a partner-managed VPC or customer's VPC; we also have KMS integration and can surface audit logs to your SIEM. I'll attach the security doc but short answer: we can keep telemetry in customer-chosen region depending on plan.
[01:36] Sara (CloudPeak): Can you share the SOC/ISO docs for the listing? Marketplace requires attestation.
[01:41] Alex (Redwood): Yes, will share SOC2 report link and our ISO attestation as part of the checklist.
[01:46] Jamal (Redwood): Also note there's a lightweight attestation we can provide for initial listing, and full compliance pack later.
[01:52] [timestamp glitch] Speaker 1: mm-hmm
[02:00] Benji (CloudPeak): On the network side we need to decide between VPC peering, PrivateLink, and transit gateway style. Which approach do you see partners use most often?
[02:08] Priya (Redwood): Typically partners use PrivateLink for SaaS-to-customer connectivity because it's simpler and avoids transitive routing issues; VPC peering is fine for dedicated setups but can get messy at scale. For marketplace deployables if you're publishing a Marketplace AMI or CloudFormation product we often provide a reference architecture that uses PrivateLink or an edge NAT for egress to the Redwood control plane. We'll draft both options.
[02:36] Mark (CloudPeak): Noted. Also curious about how we can integrate billing — does Redwood emit usage reports we can ingest? CloudPeak wants consolidated billing for marketplace purchases.
[02:47] Alex (Redwood): We provide per-token usage exports and per-route cost breakdowns; we also support webhook hooks so you can ingest usage events into your billing pipeline. We'll include example schema.
[02:59] Sara (CloudPeak): Great. For the listing assets, what do you need from us? diagrams, logos, screenshots?
[03:05] Alex (Redwood): Standard: logo svg, 1-2 screenshots, short blurb, 1-sheeter, and a reference architecture diagram (we can draft). Also technical artifacts like Terraform module, Helm chart or AMI if you want a deployable listing.
[03:19] Benji (CloudPeak): We have an internal helm chart, will that be useful?
[03:22] Priya (Redwood): Very useful — we can adapt that into our example manifests. Ideally we get a sample values.yaml and a minimal helm chart we can run in CI to validate.
[03:32] Mark (CloudPeak): On auth, we need SSO/SAML flow so partner customers can access the listing management. Does Redwood support SAML for partner admin console?
[03:40] Priya (Redwood): Yes, Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning for enterprise customers and partners. For marketplace listing management we typically integrate with partner org SSO; we'll share the SAML metadata and a test endpoint.
[03:53] [crosstalk] Alex (Redwood): One operational note — if you offer a BYO infra option, we recommend including a preflight script that validates GPU drivers, CUDA versions, and kernel/quantization support. Many customers trip on mismatched driver versions.
[04:10] Benji (CloudPeak): Good point. What about model packaging — do partners need to containerize models or can we use Redwood model registry?
[04:18] Priya (Redwood): We have an onboarding flow: you can host model weights in Redwood's model registry or provide container images. For marketplace listing we often offer two artifacts: a connector image that calls Redwood-hosted inference, and an optional self-hosted container with a small shim that conforms to our runtime API. We'll share a sample shim repo.
[04:39] Sara (CloudPeak): Are there constraints around quantized models? Some of our customers use int8 builds.
[04:44] Priya (Redwood): No problem — our runtime supports common quant formats and we have recommended quantization profiles by architecture. We'll include a compatibility matrix. Note sometimes precision impacts latency/quality, so we recommend a short perf benchmark.
[04:59] Mark (CloudPeak): Speaking of perf, would you run a benchmark for our reference workload? We want numbers to show in the listing.
[05:06] Alex (Redwood): Yes we can. Typical approach: CloudPeak shares a representative prompt set and expected qps/latency targets, Redwood runs hosted and dedicated runs and produces a benchmark report. There's usually a small profiling fee for bench runs on dedicated capacity, but hosted runs can often be done within free credits.
[05:26] Benji (CloudPeak): OK we'll prepare a sample dataset.
[05:30] [long pause / typing]
[06:00] Priya (Redwood): Quick callouts on security checklist: SSO, KMS key exchange steps, audit log export (CloudTrail or syslog), data retention policy field in listing, and SOC/ISO artifacts. We'll send a one-pager.
[06:18] Sara (CloudPeak): For co-marketing — timeline expectations? We prefer to coordinate launch on both sides.
[06:22] Alex (Redwood): Agreed. Typical cadence is: initial listing draft + security review (2 weeks), joint testing + benchmark (1-2 weeks), legal & marketplace approvals (2-3 weeks), then joint launch. So roughly 6-8 weeks from kickoff if no blockers. We can compress for high-priority deals.
[06:42] Mark (CloudPeak): Sounds reasonable. Any legal barriers for marketplace revenue share?
[06:46] Alex (Redwood): That's usually handled by marketplace terms; we'll include our standard rev-share and referral language but legal should sync to finalize.
[06:54] Benji (CloudPeak): One technical nit — how do you handle KV cache and session affinity for high QPS models in hosted mode?
[06:59] Priya (Redwood): We use a combination of request routing with sticky sessions and a distributed KV cache. If you have strict latency SLOs we can recommend dedicated capacity for hotspot customers. I'll add a short note to the architecture doc about session affinity and cache sharding.
[07:20] Mark (CloudPeak): If we do a Private deployment for some enterprise customers, how does network egress for model updates work?
[07:25] Priya (Redwood): For private deploys we ship an agent that pulls model artifacts over a secured channel; you can also opt for air-gapped mode where you transfer artifacts via secured s3 and our bootstrap tooling. We'll detail both options.
[07:40] Sara (CloudPeak): On monitoring — do you expose Prometheus metrics or traces we can ingest?
[07:45] Priya (Redwood): Yes Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces and logs, we also export token-level cost metrics so you can correlate usage and billing.
[07:55] Alex (Redwood): Let's talk deliverables — Priya, do you want to own the reference arch draft?
[08:00] Priya (Redwood): Yup I can draft a reference arch with PrivateLink + hosted option and a BYO helm chart example. I'll include notes on SAML, KMS, and monitoring endpoints.
[08:10] Mark (CloudPeak): Great. Benji will share the helm chart and AWS account.
[08:14] Benji (CloudPeak): Yep will do.
[08:16] [minor audio interference]
[08:25] Sara (CloudPeak): Marketplace listing metadata — do you need a sandbox listing ID or can we draft in your staging?
[08:31] Alex (Redwood): We have a staging marketplace; we'll create a draft and invite you. Provide logo, blurb and snips and we'll populate.
[08:38] Mark (CloudPeak): Anything else on security — endpoint auth for the marketplace connector, do you use mTLS?
[08:44] Priya (Redwood): We support mTLS for inter-service communications and JWT-based tokens for API access. For marketplace connectors we recommend mTLS for BYO infra flows.
[08:55] Alex (Redwood): I'll note that in the checklist. Also small ops ask: please include expected support SLAs so we can size Dedicated capacity for enterprise buyers.
[09:04] Mark (CloudPeak): We're thinking 99.9 for paid customers, 99.5 for trial. Is that compatible?
[09:09] Priya (Redwood): 99.9 is achievable on Dedicated with multi-AZ. We'll include recommended sizing and autoscale triggers.
[09:18] Benji (CloudPeak): Do you have a sample terraform module to wire up the PrivateLink, endpoints and route tables?
[09:23] Priya (Redwood): Yes, will share terraform snippets and a ready-to-run module.
[09:28] Alex (Redwood): Quick risk/objection section — common blockers are legal rev-share, data residency, and drive/cuda mismatches. We think we covered them but call those out in the checklist.
[09:44] Jamal (Redwood): On joint solutions, product thought: we could co-bundle a CloudPeak 'Data Connector' that pre-processes prompts and a Redwood 'Inference SKU' — would be strong for enterprise GTM. Thoughts?
[09:56] Mark (CloudPeak): Sounds good — we'd want to show an end-to-end flow: source data in CloudPeak, connector does enrichment, calls Redwood for model inferences, results stored back.
[10:06] Sara (CloudPeak): We should draft a joint solution brief for salesplay.
[10:10] Alex (Redwood): We'll coordinate on a 1-pager and a joint demo script.
[10:14] [typing / notes]
[10:40] Priya (Redwood): Anything else? If not I'll recap action items quickly.
[10:46] Mark (CloudPeak): One last question — are there any specific marketplace policies around pricing tiers for models that we should be aware of?
[10:52] Alex (Redwood): You'll want to map to per-token tiers and optional seat-based pricing if you include a UI. Marketplace typically supports listing of metered usage, but exact checkout/commit shapes differ per marketplace — we'll send a doc that maps pricing options to marketplace product types.
[11:10] Priya (Redwood): Ok quick recap of action items: Alex will send the marketplace checklist and compliance docs; Priya will draft the ref arch and share terraform/helm snippets; Benji will share AWS account and helm chart; Mark will confirm legal touchpoints; Sara will coordinate co-marketing timeline.
[11:32] Mark (CloudPeak): Sounds good, thanks all.
[11:34] Alex (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the architecture review.
[11:38] [meeting ends]
